info.bio:
Squeeze es una banda musical británica formada en Londres en 1974. Los 2 únicos componentes que permanecen desde el principio, y también compositores de la mayoría de canciones, son Chris Difford y Glenn Tilbrook. Se suele clasificar a la banda como new wave.

Además de Difford y Tilbrook, otros componentes que han ido pasando por la banda son : Jools Holland, Paul Gunn, Gilson Lavis, Harry Kakoulli, John Bentley, Paul Carrack, Don Snow, Keith Wilkinson

scenes.name: Modernismo británico: de Ultravox a U2
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Los puentes entre punk y pop sofisticado: Ultravox funde punk, el pop robótico de Kraftwerk y Roxy Music (Vienna, uno de los discos que alumbran el synth-pop); XTC perfeccionan el arte de la canción pop como nadie (Drums And Wires, English Settlement, Skylarking); Magazine, Monochrome Set, Squeeze; Japan y su dance-pop decadente; Simple Minds; y U2, el fenómeno más sensacional de las islas desde los Beatles, que unen la vehemencia del punk con el atractivo masivo del pop.

podcast.title: New Wave Powerpop
podcast.body: Squeeze is included in the list of bands associated with the new wave form of Powerpop. Their work exemplifies the genre's ability to evolve and integrate into the broader alternative rock landscape of the late 1970s and early 1980s. "We can probably include the jam, the smiths, XTC, squeeze, and the vapors."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Paul Carrack's Short Tenure and Future Role
podcast.body: Paul Carrack, who sang lead on Squeeze's biggest hit "Tempted," was only a member of the band for approximately one year and did not stay much longer. He later became the permanent lead singer for Mike + The Mechanics. "Carrack left squeeze and later joined Mike in the mechanics where he was their permanent lead singer"

xref.title: Formation and Origins
xref.body: Hot Hot Heat was formed in Victoria, BC, in 1999. Their sound was notably inspired and informed by early new wave bands such as Squeeze, Elvis Costello, and XTC. "Hot Hot Heat was formed in Victoria, BC in 1999."

xref.title: New Wave Powerpop
xref.body: The Jam are listed as one of the bands whose music, along with other acts like The Smiths and XTC, could be included in the new wave spectrum of Powerpop. Their sound contributed to the integration of Powerpop into alternative rock, demonstrating the influence of punk. "We can probably include the jam, the smiths, XTC, squeeze, and the vapors."

xref.title: New Wave Powerpop
xref.body: The Smiths are mentioned as a band whose work aligns with the new wave interpretation of Powerpop. Their inclusion signifies the genre's broadening appeal and integration into alternative rock, showcasing diverse expressions of the hooky, melodic, and energetic sound. "We can probably include the jam, the smiths, XTC, squeeze, and the vapors."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: New Wave Powerpop
xref.body: The Vapors are mentioned as a band contributing to the new wave iteration of Powerpop. Their sound, like other contemporaries, demonstrated how Powerpop's core elements were adopted and adapted within the burgeoning alternative rock scene. "We can probably include the jam, the smiths, XTC, squeeze, and the vapors."
